---
title: "Example 11: A pipeline"
engine: knitr
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(socviz)
```

## Load our packages

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-01"
#| message: TRUE
library(here)      # manage file paths
library(socviz)    # data and some useful functions
library(tidyverse) # your friend and mine
library(targets)   # pipelines
```

## A scratch project

A `targets` project has two parts: a script, `_targets.R`, that defines the
pipeline, and a data store, `_targets/`, where the results are kept. Normally
both live at the top of your project folder. Here we put them in a temporary
directory, so as not to break this website.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-02"
pipeline_dir <- fs::dir_create(fs::path_temp("organ_pipeline"))
pipeline_script <- fs::path(pipeline_dir, "_targets.R")
pipeline_store <- fs::path(pipeline_dir, "_targets")
```

## Write the pipeline

`tar_script()` writes its contents to a `_targets.R` file. The pipeline takes
the `organdata` data, drops missing values, summarizes donor rates by country,
fits a model, and draws a figure. Each step is a _target_.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-03"
tar_script(
  {
    library(targets)
    tar_option_set(packages = c("dplyr", "ggplot2", "socviz"))

    list(
      tar_target(organ_raw, organdata),
      tar_target(
        organ_clean,
        organ_raw |>
          filter(!is.na(donors), !is.na(gdp))
      ),
      tar_target(
        donor_summary,
        organ_clean |>
          summarize(
            mean_donors = mean(donors),
            sd_donors = sd(donors),
            .by = c(country, consent_law)
          )
      ),
      tar_target(
        donor_model,
        lm(donors ~ gdp + consent_law, data = organ_clean)
      ),
      tar_target(
        donor_plot,
        ggplot(
          donor_summary,
          aes(
            x = mean_donors,
            y = reorder(country, mean_donors),
            color = consent_law
          )
        ) +
          geom_pointrange(
            aes(
              xmin = mean_donors - sd_donors,
              xmax = mean_donors + sd_donors
            )
          ) +
          labs(
            x = "Donors per million population",
            y = NULL,
            color = "Consent law"
          )
      )
    )
  },
  script = pipeline_script,
  ask = FALSE
)
```

## What's in the pipeline?

`tar_manifest()` lists the targets and the command for each one.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-04"
tar_manifest(script = pipeline_script) |>
  select(name)
```

## Run it

`tar_make()` runs every target that is out of date. The first time through,
that's all of them.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-05"
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

## Read the results

Results are stored on disk. `tar_read()` fetches them.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-06"
tar_read(donor_model, store = pipeline_store) |>
  broom::tidy()
```

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-07"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
tar_read(donor_plot, store = pipeline_store)
```

## Run it again

Nothing has changed, so nothing needs to be rebuilt.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-08"
tar_outdated(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)

tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

## Change one step

Now we edit the pipeline so that the model also includes `pubhealth`. We
rewrite the script with one line changed.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-09"
pipeline_script |>
  read_lines() |>
  str_replace(
    fixed("donors ~ gdp + consent_law"),
    "donors ~ gdp + pubhealth + consent_law"
  ) |>
  write_lines(pipeline_script)
```

`targets` works out that only the model is affected. The data, the summary,
and the plot don't depend on it, so they stay as they are.

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-10"
tar_outdated(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)

tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-11"
tar_read(donor_model, store = pipeline_store) |>
  broom::tidy()
```

## Clean up

```{r}
#| label: "11-example-12"
fs::dir_delete(pipeline_dir)
```
